_comment: M14.0.SPEC (#419) — toml completeness classification. Every public NAMED node type of the pinned wasm/tree-sitter-toml.wasm is in exactly one bucket. The grammar exposes 20 nodeTypeForId slots but only 19 DISTINCT names: `escape_sequence` is declared twice, which is a grammar quirk rather than two node types. ERROR and MISSING are injected by this gate for EVERY language because the wasm ABI does not list them; neither occurs for this grammar and both are silent here. Silence is guilt: a type in no bucket fails section A, and a type the wasm no longer produces is a stale row and also fails. That rule bites hardest on the four DATETIME types — none appears anywhere in cargo's 684 files, so their handling is pinned by FIXTURE rather than by the corpus, and a corpus-only lane would have classified them by assumption and called it coverage. SECTION D IS RED AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. The gate requires >=2 distinct `evidenceClass` values and TOML has exactly ONE: every edge it emits is `structural`. YAML, the closest config-format precedent, pins four and legitimately so — a merge key is an inference, an anchor is a reference, an `!include` is a fetch. TOML has none of those constructs: no merge, no anchor, no alias, no include, no import, no reference of any kind. Its whole graph is a nesting the document literally writes. Both routes to a second tier are dishonest and neither was taken: emitting a `uses` edge for a path-shaped string imports ecosystem knowledge about which keys are paths in which tool into a format that defines no references, and tagging an edge to an IMPLIED parent as `inferred` points at a target that is deliberately not a symbol, where an edge to a non-existent node is the unresolvable-identity defect. D stays red until the gate grows a documented single-tier allowance or TOML grows a construct that earns one. E and F are the canonical F5 ceremony, exactly as for html.

handled_verified.note: Seventeen types, each read by name in src/ast/real-toml-analyzer.ts and each pinned. `document` is the walk root and supplies the module symbol's range. `table` and `table_array_element` are the two header forms — a table's node spans its WHOLE SECTION, from its `[` to the line before the next header, which is exactly the region its keys occupy, so a key's range always falls inside its table's and containment is checkable against the source. `pair` is a key/value line and its KEY is its first child, never its text. `bare_key`, `quoted_key` and `dotted_key` are the three key spellings, and the dotted form NESTS left-associatively, which is why segments are collected by walking down and unwinding. The nine value types — string, integer, float, boolean, array, inline_table and the four datetimes — are read to record `metadata.valueType`, and a value is DATA: it becomes a type label on its key, never a symbol of its own. That is the difference from the generic AST fallback this lane replaced, which published every literal as a node — 28 symbols for a ten-line Cargo.toml, 11 of whose names contained whitespace.

internal_silent.note: Three types that correctly emit nothing. `comment` is the only one this grammar emits here, and it is a literal: a comment is not an identity, and TOML has no block-comment form, so a `#` line contributes nothing to the graph. ERROR and MISSING are the universal recovery pair this gate injects for every language, and NEITHER OCCURS for this grammar: twelve deliberately malformed documents (unterminated header, key with no value, bare word as a value, a bracket-quoted key, `<>` soup) and tree-sitter-toml either recovered or rejected the input as invalid TOML without producing either node. A malformed document that IS accepted still yields a module and whatever sections parsed, so the degradation is partial rather than total. Both are `silent` for the same reason html's MISSING is — the analyzer does not read them, and a node that never exists cannot be evidence of anything.

decisions.question: Should the analyzer decode a quoted key's escapes by WALKING its `escape_sequence` child nodes, or by decoding the quoted_key's own text in pure-String?
decisions.ruling: RULED: decode the PARENT'S TEXT, in pure-String, and never walk `escape_sequence`. The two are equivalent by construction — an escape_sequence node's text is exactly the escape sequence its parent contains — so walking the children would buy nothing and cost a second pass over every quoted key. It would also put the lane's no-regex rule under pressure: the natural way to express a decode is a replacement pattern, and that rule exists because every regex literal is one more thing to audit for backtracking. The decode handles the escapes TOML defines in a key (\n, \t, \r, \", \\, \uXXXX) and passes an UNKNOWN escape through with its backslash rather than dropping it, because silently discarding half a key would invent a different identity. Measured: `"a\u0062c"` resolves to the single key `abc`, and a literal-string key takes a pure slice because a literal string has no escapes at all.
decisions.consequence: `escape_sequence` is classified HERE rather than as handled, so the type is accounted for exactly once and the reason it is not walked is on the record rather than being invisible.
